ai.s: Built a lightweight branded search front-end so the AI search pilot could be demonstrated to IMEX stakeholders without raw API calls.

ai.oc: Added a separate prefix-indexed /autocomplete endpoint (~50ms) that keeps noisy substring behaviour out of full search and surfaces clean name suggestions.
ai.pr: Lenient substring matching dragged in unrelated results (e.g. 'acc' pulling in 'ACC - Air Charter' for 'Accor'), degrading search precision.
ai.s: Routed partial-name typeahead through a dedicated fast autocomplete endpoint so over-lenient substring matching no longer floods AI search with noise.
ai.wy: Hive Requirement - search-noise blocker identified in the IMEX Qdrant pilot.

EP-49805.summary: Overlenient substring matching pulling in noise

ai.oc: Tokeniser handling was fixed so spaced and unspaced/concatenated brand-name variants resolve to the correct exhibitor in top results.
ai.pr: Spaces and special characters broke name matches - exhibitors registered without spaces did not surface when users typed the spaced form (and vice versa), a confirmed pilot blocker.
ai.s: Made AI search resilient to spacing and special-character differences so a query like 'Visit Scotland' still finds 'VisitScotland'.
ai.wy: Hive Requirement - confirmed name-matching blocker for the IMEX pilot.

EP-49807.summary: Spaces and special characters breaking name matches

ai.oc: Combined semantic similarity with ascii_folding character normalisation so common language variants and diacritic differences surface relevant results instead of zero results.
ai.pr: Searches using native-language or cultural name variants hit dead ends because multilingual endonym-exonym variants and accented characters were not recognised.
ai.s: Added cultural-name and diacritic tolerance to AI search so endonym/exonym variants (e.g. 'Italia' for 'Italy') return the right exhibitors.
ai.wy: Hive Requirement - multilingual matching gap raised in the IMEX pilot.

EP-49808.summary: No alias or multi-lingual variant handling

ai.oc: Extracted the parent/child relationship from PostgreSQL into the Qdrant payload during ingestion, enabling coordinator-exact, partner-exact, coordinator-fuzzy, partner-fuzzy ordering.
ai.pr: The coordinator/partner (parent/child) relationship was absent from the search data model, so exhibitor results could not be ranked in the intended four-tier order.
ai.s: Encoded the coordinator/partner hierarchy into AI search so exhibitor results follow a consistent parent/child ranking order.
ai.wy: Hive Requirement - hierarchy ranking requirement from the IMEX pilot.

ai.oc: Indexed the People, News, Product and Session entities in Qdrant so exact name matches surface and rank above weaker description-level matches, consistent with other entity types.
ai.pr: Only some entities were indexed, so exact person/session/product/news name matches could be outranked by similarly named companies or not appear at all.
ai.s: Extended AI search coverage by indexing People, Sessions, Products and News so name matches across all entity types rank correctly.
ai.wy: Hive Requirement - entity-coverage gap identified in the IMEX pilot.

EP-49810.summary: People, Session, Products, News entity not indexed

ai.oc: Added fallback handling so a no-results query surfaces a no-results message with 'Did you mean...?' suggestions and category prompts rather than an empty page.
ai.pr: Weak or zero-result searches showed blank dead-end pages instead of suggestions or nearby category prompts.
ai.s: Replaced empty AI-search dead-ends with helpful 'Did you mean...?' and category fallback prompts so buyers always have a next step.
ai.wy: Hive Requirement - poor recovery-state experience flagged in the IMEX pilot.

ai.oc: Cloning now uses a handler-registry + pipeline model: a new clone handler is a single new file with zero core changes, a single handler failure no longer halts the whole clone, every handler execution is logged with status/duration/error, clone logic was removed from the Events model, and the orchestrator shrank to ~50 lines.
ai.pr: Event cloning logic had become an ~800-line 'god class' with copy-paste handlers, no retry/partial recovery, no observability, implicit ordering, and no idempotency guarantee, making it hard to extend or debug and blocking team scalability.

ai.oc: PDO emulated prepares are enabled in the bootstrap, and functional.suite.yml now runs every test in its own isolated, rolled-back transaction with savepoints, without materially slowing the full suite.

ai.s: Fixed the functional test suite's root causes — Phalcon's digit-prefixed bind parameters and missing per-test transaction isolation — in one change.
ai.wy: A root-cause fix intended to resolve the PDO parameter-naming bug (EP-50624) and multiple test-isolation/stale-data tickets at once, with explicit acceptance criteria that the full suite must still run without meaningful slowdown.

ai.oc: Auto-registration handling to be changed so short-notice Speed Networking sessions are not missed by the hourly job.

ai.oc: Search API, Ingest service, and pg-listener run on ECS; the Search API sits behind an ALB with /health checks, crashed containers auto-restart, the API auto-scales on traffic, and ingest workers auto-scale on SQS queue depth.

ai.oc: DB triggers on all five entity tables push changes to an SQS queue with DLQ retry; a worker processes sync jobs and auto-scales on queue size, a scheduled full re-index runs via EventBridge, and a pre-event completeness check guards data readiness.

ai.wy: Sprint 2 of the Search & Discovery initiative to keep the index fresh and event-ready (Scalability Initiative / AI Readiness).

ai.oc: VPC/networking, ECS services, ALB, SQS, and EventBridge for the search system are defined in Terraform with remote S3+DynamoDB state, so a clean apply provisions a working environment with zero unexpected drift.

ai.s: All AWS infrastructure for the Global Search system was codified in Terraform, giving the search stack reproducible, version-controlled, drift-free environments.
ai.wy: Infrastructure-as-Code step of the Search & Discovery initiative to make the platform reproducible and auditable (Scalability Initiative / Platform Health).

ai.s: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators update a product's global fields directly, separating global data from event-scoped data.
ai.wy: Part of the API V3 migration to give partners a clean, well-structured product API and to support the new global versus event-scoped product architecture.

ai.oc: A DELETE /api/v3/products/{productId} endpoint that hard-deletes the global product and cascades removal of all event-scoped bindings (categories, custom fields, sponsorship, status) with 404 validation and a standard response envelope.
ai.pr: The Public API had no clean v3 way to delete a product globally and cascade its removal across all events, forcing integrators to manage event-level relations piecemeal without a single authoritative operation.
ai.s: A new Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators delete a product globally in one call, cascading its removal across every event automatically.
ai.wy: Part of the API V3 migration and the new global versus event-scoped product architecture, giving partners a predictable, standardized product lifecycle API.

ai.wy: Completes the CRUD surface for the event-scoped product binding under the V3 architecture.

ai.oc: Removed automatic IP-injection from generic anonymous fetches (kept only for login/getAuth), fixed the tag-set lifecycle to drop dead members and stop resetting TTL forever, cleaned up already-accumulated Redis keys, and added monitoring alarms to catch recurrence.

ai.oc: Fix identified to check each save's return value and aggregate per-row failures into the response so the reported count reflects only actually-persisted participants.

ai.oc: Fix identified to log the failed row, skip it, and continue processing rather than crashing and leaving a stale queued job.

ai.s: Fixed a bad participant row crashing the import worker and leaving the job stuck re-failing forever instead of being skipped.
ai.wy: Surfaced by a previously-skipped end-to-end test showing a real production reliability risk (stuck imports, log floods, unbounded queue growth).

EP-53138.summary: [BE Test fail] Import Participants: missing save-failure guard in ImportTask::importVisitorAction causes invalid PHQL and stale cron_task

ai.oc: A drop-in locale-aware router and link wrapper (with lint guards banning the raw APIs) eliminate the extra redirect on non-default locales, and a locale-neutral route-matching utility fixes the ~8 broken comparisons (scroll control, header search, auth modal, nav highlighting, etc.).

ai.s: Built a locale-aware navigation layer that removes an extra redirect on every non-English page view and fixes ~8 broken locale-naive comparisons across the app.
ai.wy: Surfaced while fixing an infinite invite redirect loop (EP-54331), where a locale-naive comparison escalated a harmless extra redirect into an infinite loop; a full 111-file code audit showed the pattern is widespread.

ai.oc: Synchronous assertions on asynchronously-rendered content are replaced with findBy/waitFor, and affected post/feed tests are audited for missing awaits and test isolation issues.
ai.pr: The full Vitest suite intermittently fails a small, non-deterministic set of tests (different files each run), most of which pass in isolation, undermining trust in CI results.
ai.s: Fixed flaky unit tests caused by asserting on content before it finished rendering asynchronously, restoring trust in the CI test suite.
ai.wy: Flaky tests block reliable CI signal and waste engineering time re-running or investigating false failures.

ai.oc: Screens for pre-filled profile, editable event details with auto timezone and date and file validation, and multi-select goals and event type, all saved to the event.
ai.pr: Organisers had no guided journey to confirm their profile and configure core event details when first given access.
ai.s: Delivers the multi-step organiser onboarding journey that captures profile, event details and event goals and saves them to the platform.
ai.wy: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1, helping new organisers set up events themselves.

ai.oc: An 'Add New Event' flow with clearly marked mandatory fields blocks progress until they are complete and lands the TAM on the Event Dashboard after saving.
ai.pr: There was no defined flow for a TAM to create the event entity inside a customer environment before onboarding begins.
ai.s: Lets a TAM create an event within an approved customer environment, with mandatory fields enforced, as the starting point for organiser onboarding.
ai.wy: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1; the event must exist before the organiser can be onboarded.

ai.oc: A 'Send Onboarding Email' option and popup with send or skip appear for the first admin user, disappear after use, and the email link redirects to Screen 1.
ai.pr: There was no in-platform way to invite an organiser admin into the onboarding journey.
ai.s: Lets a TAM send a one-time onboarding email to an organiser admin, whose link opens the first screen of the onboarding journey.
ai.wy: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1, kicking off self-service event setup.

ai.oc: The dashboard shows registered and checked-in attendees, exhibitors, sessions, speakers and total leads, plus Team Members and Selected Modules widgets.
ai.pr: After onboarding, organisers had no single landing view of event performance and their chosen modules.
ai.s: Lands organisers on an Event Dashboard after onboarding, showing real-time attendee, exhibitor, session, speaker and lead counts.
ai.wy: Part of Organizer Onboarding v1, giving organisers immediate value after setup.

ai.oc: App behaviour is updated so the floor plan display correctly reflects the organizer's current ExpoFP setting.
ai.pr: After an organizer disables the ExpoFP floor plan for an event, the Android app keeps displaying it until the user also turns off dynamic linking, which is unexpected and confusing.
ai.s: Fixed the Android app so it stops showing the ExpoFP floor plan after an organizer disables it, instead of only reacting to a separate dynamic-linking toggle.
ai.wy: Reported behaviour mismatch between the organizer's configured setting and what the app actually displays.

ai.oc: On both iOS and Android, the Terms of Use link opens in an external browser without disturbing the current registration screen, and returning users find their progress intact.
ai.pr: Tapping Terms of Use replaced the registration web-view, so mobile users lost their in-progress registration when they viewed the terms and came back.
ai.s: During mobile registration, tapping Terms of Use now opens it in the device's external browser instead of hijacking the registration web-view.
ai.wy: Prioritised via product discovery (PBV11-378) to remove a progress-loss friction point in the revenue-adjacent mobile registration flow.

ai.oc: On iOS and Android the bottom sheet lists exhibitors by company name, then sessions by title, both alphabetically.
ai.pr: Tapping or searching a floorplan location showed exhibitors and sessions mixed together, making it hard to tell companies from scheduled content.
ai.s: Groups the mobile floorplan bottom sheet with exhibitors first and sessions second, each sorted alphabetically, matching the web experience.
ai.wy: Aligns the mobile floorplan with the web and improves usability during the live event.

ai.oc: iOS and Android are checked for placeholder rendering, pick-up of disable and re-enable, local cache clearing and the category-change delta sync case.

ai.oc: Options are resolving from row data already loaded, batched pre-loading, or a category-defaults fast path for simple settings such as logo.

ai.oc: A complete list of endpoints with changed access/contract (path, what changed, condition, originating ticket) handed to the frontend team, plus an agreed and documented 401/403/404 convention applied consistently and reflected in Swagger.
ai.pr: Security hardening (e.g. EP-46843) silently changed access control on public frontend API endpoints (like `products/images`), breaking frontend caching assumptions without frontend being informed; error-code usage across the API is also inconsistent (403 vs 401 vs 404 used interchangeably for similar cases).
ai.s: Catalogued every API endpoint whose access rules silently changed during the security hardening story and defined a consistent 401/403/404 convention going forward.
ai.wy: A frontend team already hit confusion from an endpoint 'suddenly requiring a token'; this formalizes what changed across the whole pentest story so it doesn't keep causing surprises.

ai.oc: In progress: a polled, OAuth2, external-ID-matched inbound integration with four flows (account and exhibitor set/delete), team-member matching, delta cursors, and full field mappings, running on the Integration Hub AutoUpdate engine.

ai.s: A new inbound Swoogo integration automatically syncs registrants, speakers, and exhibitors, deduplicated by company, including cancellations.
ai.wy: Part of the strategic Integration Hub programme to expand EP's native connector ecosystem and remove onboarding friction for clients on third-party registration platforms.

ai.oc: In progress: an Admin Panel constructor with a toggleable hero image (upload/default/delete), title (max 50) and description (max 120) fields, flip-sides layout, per-language entry, and save/cancel with unsaved-changes protection.

ai.s: Organisers can now brand the Participant Registration welcome page (hero image, title, description, per language) via a visual constructor.

ai.s: Organisers can now brand the Buyer Registration welcome page (hero image, title, description, per language) via a visual constructor.
ai.wy: Part of the New Registration development programme, extending self-service welcome-page branding to the buyer registration flow.

EP-54657.summary: Story 2. Main Buyer registration page setup

ai.oc: Organizers can toggle a custom Website Builder page or configure image, title/description (with merge variables and rich text), an optional script, flip-sides layout, full multilanguage support, and unsaved-changes protection for the Participant confirmation experience.

ai.s: Gave organizers full self-service control over the branded Confirmation page Participants see after registering, as part of the New Registration platform rebuild.

EP-54658.summary: Story 3. Confirmation page setup for Participant

ai.oc: Organizers can toggle a custom Website Builder page or configure image, title/description (with merge variables and rich text), an optional script, flip-sides layout, full multilanguage support, and unsaved-changes protection for the Buyer confirmation experience.
ai.pr: As part of the New Registration platform rebuild, organizers had no way to customize what Buyers see immediately after registering, limiting how branded and informative that moment could be.
ai.s: Extended the self-service branded Confirmation page capability to the Buyer registration flow, as part of the New Registration platform rebuild.
ai.wy: A core piece of the New Registration development effort (RAAS), extending the Participant confirmation-page capability to the Buyer registration flow.

EP-54659.summary: Story 4. Confirmation page setup for Buyer

ai.oc: Organizers can configure an image, title/description text, and a customizable-destination call-to-action button for the Sold Out page, with flip-sides layout and multilanguage support.
ai.pr: When all tickets for an event sell out, there was no defined branded experience to show Participants attempting to register, only an ad hoc or generic dead end.
ai.s: Let organizers configure a branded 'Sold Out' page with a customizable call-to-action button, so a fully-booked event no longer dead-ends registrants.
ai.wy: Part of the New Registration development effort (RAAS), ensuring a sold-out event still gives Participants a clear, branded, actionable message instead of a broken flow.

EP-54661.summary: Story 5. Sold out tickets page setup

ai.oc: A configurable Sold Out page (organizer-set image/title/description/button, default copy, flip-sides layout, multilanguage) that appears before or after email validation whenever no visible tickets remain.
ai.pr: When all tickets visible to a participant (by category/country) were sold out, the old registration flow had no dedicated, organizer-brandable page to explain this and redirect the visitor.
ai.s: New Registration adds a branded, organizer-configurable Sold Out page so attendees get clear guidance instead of a confusing dead end when tickets run out.
ai.wy: Part of the planned New Registration (RAASS) rebuild; needed so the new flow has full parity with, and improves on, legacy sold-out handling.

ai.oc: Attendees with paid items are redirected to the existing Payment page on submit, except Private Events with public access or where the registration limit is reached, where items go to the Basket instead; an item-availability check runs before payment.
ai.pr: The new registration flow needed defined, consistent logic for when a paid booking triggers immediate payment versus deferred Basket payment, across normal, private-with-public-access, and registration-limit-reached cases.
ai.s: New Registration reliably routes paid bookings to payment (or a deferred Basket in two exception cases) so ticket and session revenue is actually collected.
ai.wy: Required for the New Registration rebuild to preserve revenue-critical payment completion behaviour from the legacy flow.

ai.oc: A new landing page with email verification that blocks duplicates, triggers Repeated Registration or Continue Unfinished Registration flows as appropriate, and is multilingual.
ai.pr: Without an email-first landing step, visitors could start registering with duplicate, already-used, or previously-abandoned emails, creating messy or duplicate registration data.
ai.s: A new email-verification landing page catches duplicate and unfinished registrations before an attendee even starts the form.
ai.wy: Needed for the New Registration rebuild to gate entry into the form and route visitors to the correct flow.

EP-54664.summary: Story 8. Registration: Visitor can verify Email on Registration Landing Page

ai.oc: A Buyer Registration Landing Page with email verification, duplicate-Buyer blocking, identity verification for existing Participants, and routing to Repeated/Unfinished Registration flows; skipped entirely for logged-in Participant-to-Buyer upgrades.
ai.pr: Buyer registration (reached via Agent-shared links) had no equivalent email-first gate, so duplicate Buyers or unverified Participant-to-Buyer upgrades were possible.
ai.s: Buyer Registration gets its own email-verification landing page, with identity checks so only valid, unique emails reach the Buyer flow.
ai.wy: Companion story to Story 8, required for consistent New Registration behaviour across Participant and Buyer flows.

EP-54665.summary: Story 9. Registration: Visitor can verify Email on Buyer Registration Landing Page

ai.oc: Simple Registration settings, its custom-script hook, and all related UI/logic are removed; every event always goes through the standard Summary-page flow.
ai.pr: Simple Registration (a legacy flow that skipped the Summary page) had not been used by any customer for years but remained in the codebase and Admin Panel, adding maintenance surface and inconsistent behaviour.
ai.s: Simple Registration, unused by any customer for years, is removed so the platform keeps a single consistent registration flow.
ai.wy: Business decision to discontinue an unused legacy option so the platform has one consistent registration flow going into the New Registration rebuild.

ai.oc: A mandatory Tickets tab with category-based filtering, multi-ticket purchases, a 1-hour reservation hold, sold-out handling, and pre-selected-category URL support.
ai.pr: Ticket purchasing needed to be rebuilt as a mandatory, category-aware step inside the new registration pipeline, replicating and improving legacy ticketing behaviour.
ai.s: Ticket selection and purchase is rebuilt as a mandatory, category-aware registration step with reservation holds, directly powering ticket revenue.
ai.wy: Core commerce step of the New Registration rebuild — tickets are the primary paid item most events sell.

EP-54667.summary: Story 11. Registration: Participant can select and purchase Tickets during Registration

ai.oc: Grids and their fields show/hide based on Participant Category or conditional-question answers, hidden tabs disappear entirely, and requiredness on hidden fields is ignored until they become visible again.
ai.pr: The new registration UI lacked the conditional-visibility logic (by category or by answer) that the legacy registration and the new Edit Profile already supported, so forms could not adapt to different attendee types.
ai.s: Registration forms now show or hide grids and fields based on category or prior answers, so attendees only see what applies to them.
ai.wy: Required for feature parity with legacy Registration and consistency with the new Edit Profile experience.

EP-54668.summary: Story 12. Registration: Condition logic for Grids and Fields during Registration

ai.oc: A side navigation menu (event image/logo, tab list, Order Summary of paid items) with Previous/Next buttons, tab-click navigation restricted to visited tabs, and required-field gating; Order Summary hidden on mobile widths.
ai.pr: The new registration UI needed navigation between tabs (buttons and tab clicks) with required-field gating and a visible summary of what's being purchased, matching the legacy behaviour and new design.
ai.s: A new side navigation menu with tab navigation and a live order summary gives attendees clear progress and pricing visibility during registration.
ai.wy: Core navigation shell required for the New Registration rebuild to be usable at all.

ai.oc: Grids/Fields/Info Frames render with full attribute support (required, sensitive, hidden, disabled, not editable, conditional, timestamp capture); Email/Country/Category system fields auto-populate and lock; data pre-saves across tab navigation.
ai.pr: The new registration UI needed its form rendering (fields, attributes like required/hidden/disabled, and system-field pre-population) to match legacy Registration and the new Edit Profile visually and functionally.
ai.s: Registration's form fields now render and auto-populate exactly like the new Edit Profile, with full support for required, hidden and disabled attributes.
ai.wy: Foundational rendering layer needed for every other registration tab in the New Registration rebuild.

ai.oc: A Sessions tab with search/filters, paid and free session booking, seat-availability enforcement, and organizer-configured "at least one" or "all sessions" required rules.
ai.pr: Session booking needed to move from a post-registration profile action into the registration pipeline itself, with support for organizer rules requiring at least one or all sessions to be selected.
ai.s: Sessions can now be searched, filtered and booked (paid or free) directly during registration, capturing session revenue earlier in the funnel.
ai.wy: Extends the New Registration commerce surface beyond tickets to sessions, another paid item type.

EP-54671.summary: Story 15. Sessions as part of Registration

ai.oc: A Summary page showing all in-scope tab data with Edit links, paid items with discount-code support, unavailable-item warnings, T&Cs/reCAPTCHA, and a context-aware "Proceed to payment"/"Submit" button.
ai.pr: The new registration flow needed a final review step that shows all submitted data and paid items, supports discount codes, and gives a clear next action (submit vs. pay), matching the legacy Basket discount logic.
ai.s: A consolidated Summary page with discount codes, pricing, and validation is the final review step before registration payment or submission.
ai.wy: Final checkpoint of the New Registration pipeline, required before payment or submission can occur.

ai.oc: A Terms and Conditions step with a detail pop-up, required-agreement enforcement with a blocking snackbar, and a confirmation snackbar on acceptance.
ai.pr: The new registration UI lacked a Terms and Conditions gate, needed for organizers who legally require attendee agreement before completing sign-up.
ai.s: Registration now enforces Terms and Conditions agreement before completion, giving organizers the legal compliance step the old flow had.
ai.wy: Legal/compliance requirement carried over from legacy Registration, mandatory for organizers who enable it.

ai.oc: Confirmation, waitlist, pending-approval and other Registration-triggered emails fire with the same content, recipients and trigger conditions as the legacy flow, using existing organizer-configured templates.
ai.pr: Migrating to New Registration risked silently dropping or changing email notifications participants and organizers rely on.
ai.s: All legacy registration emails (confirmation, waitlist, pending-approval) are replicated in the new flow so no attendee or organizer communication is lost.
ai.wy: Parity requirement to avoid a communication regression when the new registration flow replaces the old one.

ai.oc: Self Registration's Admin Panel settings, frontend pages, and backend logic are removed; legacy URLs redirect appropriately, with no impact to standard, Buyer, or other registration flows.
ai.pr: Self Registration was a redundant legacy feature adding maintenance overhead and complexity alongside the new consolidated registration flow.
ai.s: The legacy Self Registration feature is fully removed, leaving one supported registration flow and less code to maintain.
ai.wy: Cleanup decision to reduce the number of parallel registration code paths ahead of the New Registration rollout.

ai.oc: A category embedded in the Registration URL filters the Ticketing page to that category (plus "available for all") and pre-fills/locks the Category field on Contact Details, falling back to standard behaviour on invalid category IDs.
ai.pr: Organizers sending category-specific registration links had no way to make the URL pre-filter tickets and lock the category field, forcing attendees to re-select what the link already implied.
ai.s: Category-specific registration links now pre-filter tickets and lock the category field, streamlining targeted registration for attendees.
ai.wy: Streamlines targeted registration links (e.g. sent by sales/agents) as part of the New Registration rebuild.

EP-54676.summary: Story 20. Embed Participant Category in Registration URLs

ai.oc: A Confirmation page rendering organizer-configured image/text with dynamic variables (name, email, barcode, QR code, badge link, etc.), executing organizer scripts, supporting a full custom-page override, and multilanguage switching.
ai.pr: The new registration flow needed a post-completion confirmation page supporting the same dynamic variables, custom scripts and multilanguage content as legacy Registration.
ai.s: A personalised Confirmation page with dynamic badge/QR/name variables and organizer scripts closes out the new registration flow.
ai.wy: Closing step of the New Registration pipeline, required for parity with legacy confirmation behaviour.

ai.oc: A Buyer-specific Confirmation page with organizer-configured image/text, dynamic variables (name, email, barcode, QR code, badge link), script execution, custom-page override, and multilanguage support.
ai.pr: Buyer Registration needed its own confirmation page with the same dynamic-variable and custom-script support as the Participant flow, rather than sharing an inconsistent or missing experience.
ai.s: Buyers now get their own personalised Confirmation page with dynamic details, mirroring the Participant confirmation experience.
ai.wy: Companion story to Story 21, required for full Buyer Registration parity in the New Registration rebuild.

ai.oc: Visitors on Public Events complete registration and self-activate via an emailed activation link, with registration-limit, repeated-registration, unfinished-registration and payment flows all wired in.
ai.pr: The New Registration pipeline needed to fully support the most common case, Public Events, including email verification, activation, and payment for paid items, without regressing existing behaviour.
ai.s: The default, highest-volume Public Event registration path — signup, activation and payment — is fully rebuilt in the new registration pipeline.
ai.wy: This is the default/most-used registration path and a prerequisite for shipping New Registration at all.

ai.oc: Participants submit registration pending organizer approval; paid items are reserved and payment is deferred to a forced, un-closable Basket shown after activation, on web and mobile.

ai.oc: The integrity check is fixed to treat `fileHash` as an ETag (skipping/adapting strict MD5 comparison for multipart or malformed values), the primary-download gate is fixed so a clean install still triggers the first download, and failures no longer report false success.
